subject: BrightByte POC: orchestration slot + token throughput targets
messages:
From: Sam Nguyen <sam@brightbyte.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - performance deep-dive request

Hi Rafael / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to kick off a performance deep-dive prior to the production pilot — primarily to validate token throughput and tail latency under our traffic shape. High level asks: 
- Sustained target: ~15,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across the cluster) for steady-state daytime traffic.
- Burst/peak target: ~60,000 tokens/sec for short spikes (1-3 minute windows).
- Latency goal: p95 < 220ms for short-context requests (~64 tokens).

Can we schedule a 90-minute technical runbook session to align on: load profile, sequence lengths, concurrency model, exact model variant to serve, and what artifacts BrightByte will share (traces, sample payloads)? Ideally next week (Mar 23-26) in the morning PST. We can also provide a 30-minute production trace sample and a small replay harness.

I'll attach a short doc with our expected traffic classes. Let me know availability and any specific infra constraints on your side.

— Sam
Sam Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightByte
sam@brightbyte.ai
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam@brightbyte.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - performance deep-dive request

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to run the deep-dive.

A few quick clarifying items before we lock a slot:
- Which model variant are you planning to test (fp16 / int8 / custom-tunable)? That impacts quantization paths and kernel choices.
- Typical generation length distribution (median / 90th percentile token lengths) and the percentage of multi-turn requests vs single prompt.
- Do you want Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for the run, or should we use Hosted with burst fallback? Dedicated makes repeatability easier for SLO testing.

Proposed 90-minute windows (PST):
- Wed Mar 24, 09:30–11:00
- Thu Mar 25, 10:00–11:30

I've attached a baseline loadtest plan (loadtest-plan-v1.xlsx) and a quick network/poC map (brightbyte_poc_map.pdf) that outline where we need traces and what instrumentation we'll enable.

If you confirm the model and upload one representative trace (S3/Drive link is fine), we can pre-generate replay scripts and pre-reserve a small dedicated pool for the workshop.

Thanks — cc'ing Laura for scheduling and infra constraints.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
[attachment: loadtest-plan-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[attachment: brightbyte_poc_map.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Nguyen <sam@brightbyte.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-23T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - performance deep-dive request

Looping in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (OPS) so we can coordinate capacity windows and runbook owners.

Quick notes from scheduling/ops: 
- We have a maintenance blackout for Dedicated pool changes on Wed 03/24 from 06:00–09:00 PDT, so the earlier Wed window is tight. Thu 03/25 10:00–11:30 looks cleaner.
- We can provision a 3-GPU dedicated pool for the rehearsal; for the full load test you'll want more — we'll confirm numbers after we see the trace.
- Please upload the production trace sample as a gzipped jsonl (prod-trace-sample.jsonl.gz) or share a Drive link and we'll pull it into our replay harness.

Marissa: can you tentatively reserve Thu 03/25 10:00–11:30 PDT for the workshop and mark the runbook owner?

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Sam Nguyen <sam@brightbyte.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-23T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - performance deep-dive request

Thanks — Thu 03/25 10:00–11:30 PDT works for us.

Answers to clarifying questions:
- Model: we'll test the open-llm-7b variant (int8 preferred). We'll include a small set of fp16 baselines.
- Lengths: median gen ~48 tokens, p90 ~180 tokens. ~65% single-turn inference, 35% multi-turn (2–4 exchanges).
- We'll upload a 30-minute sampled trace (prod-trace-sample.jsonl) to the Drive folder now: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/brightbyte-poc
- We can start with Dedicated 3-GPU pool for the workshop and scale to 12 GPUs for the full stress run after we baseline.

Attachments: I dropped a trimmed trace (prod-trace-sample.jsonl) and a short doc with traffic classes in the Drive folder.

Sam
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam@brightbyte.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-25T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Confirmed: BrightByte POC — Thu Mar 25 10:00–11:30 PDT (performance deep-dive)

Sam / team — confirmed slot and next steps. Calendar invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123

Agenda (90 min):
1) 10m — Introductions & success criteria (p95 latency / token throughput targets)
2) 20m — Trace shape review and playback plan (we'll show the replay script we generated from your trace)
3) 30m — Live rehearsal on Dedicated 3-GPU pool (steady-state and controlled bursts)
4) 20m — Scaling plan: how we'll scale to 12 GPUs for stress window & metric interpretation
5) 10m — Actions & ownership (rollout plan, artifacts we ship)

Pre-work (please complete before Thu 03/25 08:00 PDT):
- BrightByte: confirm final replay trace file name in the Drive folder.
- Redwood: we'll pre-generate the replay harness and upload the initial reports to the Drive folder.
- Both: add any test credentials to the shared secret vault link in the Drive folder.

Attachments: loadtest-plan-v1.xlsx (initial test plan), brightbyte_poc_map.pdf, prod-trace-sample.jsonl referenced.

Action items assigned:
- Rafael: produce replay harness and test scripts (PR to internal repo).
- Karthik: reserve Dedicated 3-GPU pool and validate network egress.
- Marissa: runbook owner for the workshop and postmortem notes.
- Sam: upload final trace and confirm S3/Drive permissions.

If anything changes, reply-all and we'll reschedule. Looking forward to it.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
